newsitem.title: ITALY: Upgraded handling could cut Italian airfreight trucking.
newsitem.headline: Upgraded handling could cut Italian airfreight trucking.

text.p: Upgrading handling facilities at Italy's main cargo airports --Malpensa and Fiumicino -- to provide an efficient airfreight service for northern and southern Italy could reduce trucking to other European airports, Alitalia cargo executive, Fulvio Neri said.
He told a parliamentary sub-committee that a Freight Leaders Club study showed northern Italy accounted for 74 percent of Italian air cargo exports, with Milan's two airports handling 59 percent.
However 70 percent of northern Italy's exports are trucked to airports elsewhere in Europe for shipment due to the lack of an adequate logistics handling system at Malpensa.
Bureaucratic procedures also means it takes at least 24 hours to release cargo at Italian airports, compared to an average three to four hours elsewhere in Europe, Neri said.
Air cargo shipped from New York to Venice will thus arrive earlier at its destination if it is flown to Frankfurt and then trucked south, rather than being flown to Milan.
Neri told the subcommittee that improved security systems should be introduced to protect airfreight in Italy from the highest levels in Europe of "plunder, theft and damage".

Standardised procedures to overcome the bureaucratic delays faced by air cargo together with a more structured approach to meeting the market's needs should also be introduced, he said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
